summary.intent: Execute Phase 50 (IPFS/IPNS Data-Integrity Fixes) via /gsd-manager, implementing five fix plans across parallel worktrees to resolve data-loss bugs: INT_MIN advisory-lock hash overflow, re-pinned CID drain race, and incomplete IPNS unenrollment for unloaded subtrees.
summary.outcome: Phase 50 fully executed, code-reviewed, simplified, security-cleared, validated (Nyquist-compliant), and shipped as PR #527. All code-review blockers (cycle guard, catch handlers, TOCTOU lock fixes) were applied pre-ship; CodeRabbit and Greptile post-PR findings were also resolved with 3 additional commits.

repo: pnpm/orval resolves to the workspace root (not the worktree root) when run inside a git worktree, so `pnpm api:generate` leaks 131 generated api-client files into the orchestrator's working tree instead of staying isolated
Husky regenerates .husky/_/ hook stubs during `pnpm install` inside worktrees, showing up as untracked files in the orchestrator after merge
The `gsd_run query commit` helper reports `commit_failed` even when the commit succeeds — always verify with `git log` after a false-negative

The wave cleanup helper returns opaque `merge_failed` with empty stderr when the pre-commit hook (lint-staged across 137 api-client files) stalls during its internal commit; manual `git merge && git commit` with hooks enabled succeeds
The dep-string 'Phase 49 (v1.1 baseline)' gets mis-parsed by GSD tools into a phantom phase '1.1', marking deps unsatisfied even when Phase 49 is complete
todos/done/ (70 items) is a legacy folder — GSD tooling references todos/completed/ exclusively; the two drifted after a June 15 GSD update. Consolidated to completed/ in this session
PR titles must follow Conventional Commits (no parens); pr-title.yml CI rejects the default 'Phase N: Name' format — use `fix:` or `feat:` instead
`gh` commands require `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN` in this repo; release-please commits to the base branch immediately after PR creation, requiring fetch+rebase before pushing any tracking commits
Greptile declines to review PRs with >240 files — 131 api-client regenerated files reliably trigger this limit
CodeRabbit posts post-PR nitpicks in the review body, not as inline threads — /resolve-pr-reviews must parse pulls/N/reviews[].body

`pg_advisory_xact_lock` accepts signed bigint; int4→bigint sign-extends safely, so `abs(hashtext($1)::int4)` was wrong — INT_MIN (-2147483648) overflowed abs(), making that CID's hash permanently wrong and the CID undeletable

code.finding: `rowDeleted = true` was set unconditionally after `pinnedCidRepo.delete()`, so `fileUnpins.inc()` fired even on 0-row deletes (lost-race path). Fixed to gate on `deleteResult.affected > 0` (IN-01 regression, caught by CodeRabbit post-PR).

New `collectSubtreeIpnsNamesAsync` function had no `visited` Set — folder-metadata cycles (attacker-influenceable client-supplied data) caused unbounded recursion. Fixed by mirroring the `ensureFolderLoaded` DFS cycle guard pattern (CR-01).

The catch-block `!visited.has(entry.ipnsName)` guard is NOT dead code (Greptile false positive). The recursive call at line 357 mutates `visited`+`acc` before potentially throwing on malformed `children`; the guard deduplicates on diamond or post-throw re-entry.

JSDoc overstated that the advisory lock 'closes the WR-01 race window' against `recordPin`; `recordPin` never takes the lock. The residual drain↔recordPin sub-window is cryptographically negligible (D-13: byte-identical ciphertext+IV required). Comment corrected per Greptile finding.
Refcount guard added by plan 50-02: checks `pinnedCidRepository.count` before calling `unpinFile`, skipping physical unpin when CID is re-pinned (count > 0) to prevent Kubo GC data loss.

workflow: Parallel worktree execution (4 Wave 1 plans) ran in ~15 min wall-clock vs ~40 min sequential; verify `shouldDegrade: false` and that base commit contains PLAN files before dispatch

Wave merge order for a pre-commit-hook-heavy repo: run cleanup-wave helper first; on opaque `merge_failed`, inspect dirty state, verify all plan files are committed, clean regenerated artifacts, then do manual `git merge && git commit` with hooks enabled
Run targeted test suites (per-package jest/vitest on changed files) after phase merge rather than full parallel monorepo suite to avoid RAM exhaustion

CodeRabbit CLI (`coderabbit review --agent --base-commit <sha>`) can pre-screen findings before PR creation; `until` poll loop on `gh api pulls/N/reviews` reliably detects when the post-PR bot review completes

DFS cycle guards in recursive tree traversal should be added at the same time as the recursive function — `ensureFolderLoaded` had one; `collectSubtreeIpnsNamesAsync` missed it until code review, highlighting a review pattern to watch for when adding new recursive tree walkers

Post-PR resolve-pr-reviews workflow: fetch review bodies + inline comments, verify each finding against live code before applying, reason through false positives explicitly (e.g. Greptile's 'dead guard' claim), push with fetch+rebase for release-please bot commit
